description: Machine-readable workflow contract for brand learning and host apply. The contract keeps Brand native, borrows external orchestration ideas when useful, and prevents Markdown-only rules from becoming fake gates.

levels.L2: Consumer contract may reject incomplete or semantically unsafe inputs.
levels.L3: Pipeline integration traces Screenshot -> Claim -> Pattern -> Demo selector/state.
levels.L4: Blind QA independently reviews source and rendered output without implementation rationale.

nodeQualityModel.failureRule: Route every failure to the earliest node where the claim first became incorrect; fixing only the final symptom does not close the incident.
nodeQualityModel.closureRule: Close only after corrective action, preventive gate, recapture, fresh Blind QA, and regression pass.

roleCapabilityModel.purpose: Make every subagent independently dispatchable and reject role-shaped prose that cannot be verified at handoff.
roleCapabilityModel.crossCheckRule: Producer self-check is necessary but never sufficient. The named downstream consumer or fresh QA must reject incomplete coverage, semantic expansion, or unverifiable rendered claims.
roleCapabilityModel.scopeRule: A role reports completion only for its declared scope. A journey, page, component family, or state PASS must never be promoted to full-host PASS without a zero-gap host coverage matrix.

minimumCompetencies.evidenceReasoning: Distinguish observed rendered facts, code-discovered candidates, inference, unresolved evidence, and unavailable evidence.
minimumCompetencies.semanticReasoning: Preserve the narrowest evidence-backed role and keep business semantics separate from brand expression.
minimumCompetencies.implementationReasoning: Consume approved ids and matrices, verify real DOM/computed/interaction results, and preserve host business behavior.
minimumCompetencies.qualityReasoning: Test visible user outcomes across route, branch, state, family, language, viewport, and journey instead of accepting representative nodes.
minimumCompetencies.methodologyReasoning: Convert repeated mechanisms into tested gates while keeping one-brand accidents as candidates.

roleCapabilityModel.programObjective: Prove a reusable two-pipeline system: learn-brand derives an evidence-backed, generative brand model; design-host applies that frozen model to a real host while preserving business behavior. A branded host screenshot or a page-level CSS change is evidence for one slice, never the objective itself.
roleCapabilityModel.progressRule: Report progress at its native hierarchy level. Never convert host coverage-cell completion into learn-brand completion or overall two-pipeline completion. The twoPipelineProgram passes only when both pipelines independently pass their required gates and a second held-out brand/host transfer proves reuse.
roleCapabilityModel.antiProxyRule: Do not use changed CSS files, screenshot count, build success, route count, representative components, or host coverage percentages as a proxy for reusable pipeline completion.

hostCoverageMatrix.requiredFor: Every apply-host implementation and final sign-off.
rules: Every discovered route, reachable branch, meaningful state, component-family variant and required viewport receives an explicit matrix cell.
Every child route records parentRoute and launchedFrom; its parent/default entry also needs a covered navigation cell.
KEEP means intentionally preserved with rationale and acceptance evidence, never no design responsibility.
DEFER remains visible debt and prevents fullHost PASS unless it is explicitly outside the frozen goal.

CJK typography cells record the actual text sample and computed family, weight, size, line-height and letter-spacing; a Latin display face cannot be the only family for Chinese text without an approved exception.
Interactive cells measure the real hit-test owner, not only a wrapper, and require at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels unless an explicit platform exception is approved.
Semantic color cells identify businessSemantic, brandRole, allowedRoles and antiScopes so PVP, type, status, price or inventory colors are not silently replaced.
fullHost PASS requires every in-scope cell PASS, default entry coverage, all parent launch paths covered, and no in-scope DEFER or missing family variant.

Evidence promotion is transactional: a QA batch verdict does not update cells unless every promoted cell id has an explicit evidence reference and the stored coverageSummary exactly matches recomputed cell totals.

previewBlockerCodes.MOCKUP_SHELL_MISSING: A standard-demo page does not visibly render the phone mockup shell; DOM classes alone are insufficient when computed frame border/radius or screenshots show the shell has been removed.
previewBlockerCodes.CALIBRATION_SURFACE_LEAKED: No-shell calibration CSS is active on a normal user-facing Demo route instead of being isolated behind an explicit proof mode.
previewBlockerCodes.HOME_INDICATOR_LAYOUT_LEAK: The mockup home indicator participates in page layout, moves with content, compresses the phone screen, or appears as an appended footer instead of a fixed system overlay.
previewBlockerCodes.MULTI_MODULE_PAGE_SECTIONS_MISSING: Long-page or multi-module evidence exists, but the preview declares fewer than two schema sections.
previewBlockerCodes.PAGE_NOT_SCROLLABLE: A required long/multi-module phone screen does not have scrollHeight > clientHeight or scrollTop cannot change.
previewBlockerCodes.PAGE_SCROLL_NOT_RESTORED: The browser scroll probe changed a required phone screen but could not restore its original scrollTop.

hostStructuralDiffGate.baselineRule: The Design Director / Orchestrator captures every route target through prepare-bundle before Host Implementation dispatch. The bundle freezes route, source file, source SHA-256, baseline file, baseline SHA-256, timestamp and owner. An after-the-fact or producer-authored snapshot is invalid evidence.
hostStructuralDiffGate.approvalRule: Decorative additions need evidence; primitive/component substitutions need explicit product/design approval and may not be self-approved by Host Implementation.

brandDistinctivenessGate.requiredFor: Every apply-host visual QA; high-capacity pages use the strict material-signal rules.
brandDistinctivenessGate.evidenceRule: Compare source and host screenshots captured at the same declared viewport. Masked review must score design-system structural recognition separately from explicit-IP recognition; a reviewer must never be asked to infer a specific IP solely from business data or hidden identity marks.
brandDistinctivenessGate.highCapacityRule: At least three visible evidence-backed signals, each occupying at least five percent of the viewport, spanning at least three dimensions. Typography, micro-icons, logos, brand names and other small signatures cannot satisfy this requirement.

recognitionModel.designSystemStructuralRecognition: Required by default. Tests whether evidence-backed token roles, component grammar, composition and asset placement form the learned design system while host business content remains intact.
recognitionModel.explicitIpRecognition: Diagnostic by default. It becomes a blocking gate only when the frozen goal explicitly requires IP identification and authorizes the necessary identity-bearing assets or copy.
recognitionModel.noSilentDowngrade: Changing either recognition track from blocking to diagnostic, or changing a frozen threshold, requires a goal-contract revision and an explicit supersession record; QA and Implementation cannot do this after seeing a result.

brandDistinctivenessGate.nonCompensationRule: Technical gates and business safety never compensate for visualDistinctiveness FAIL. Never publish a single overall completion percentage.

programStrategyGate.requiredBefore: Host Implementation dispatch and every two-pipeline progress report.
rules: The program goal tree reports learn-brand, design-host and held-out reuse as separate branches with their own status, evidence, remaining gap and next action.
Host coverage percentages remain evidence for design-host implementation scope and cannot become the two-pipeline program percentage.
Every host page records business purpose plus token, component, composition and asset decisions.
Every page declares Hero eligibility with a business reason; eligible is not equivalent to required.
Recognition policy names structural and explicit-IP tracks and preserves the frozen blocking/diagnostic policy.

policy: Brand domain routing, DTCG mapping, DangoUI contract checks, host placement decisions, and final coverage wording stay inside Brand Skill.
External projects such as gstack may inspire role orchestration, review style, and retro discipline, but they must not replace Brand blocking gates.
When an external goodcase overlaps with an existing Brand capability, classify it as retain, iterate, deprecate, or optional-hook before editing files.

rules: Design Director / Orchestrator is the top-level accountable agent, not a sequential subagent stage.
The top-level agent owns goal freeze, work decomposition, design-direction.json, dispatch, failure routing and final sign-off.
Freeze and hash the goal contract before dispatching Evidence.
Each subagent stage receives only the allowed inputs declared by its role contract.
After Interpreter passes, the top-level agent must create and validate design-direction.json before Demo can be dispatched.
The Demo and Visual QA stages must use different agent execution ids.
Visual QA must run in a fresh context and must not receive implementation rationale, prior verdicts, or desired wording.
A QA failure returns only the frozen goal and blocking findings to Demo; it never changes the goal or thresholds.
Demo may retry twice. Every retry requires a new demo screenshot hash and a new Visual QA execution id.
Scripts validate dispatch receipts and gates; scripts do not pretend to spawn Codex subagents themselves.
Learn-brand Demo is a brand-learning-capability-test, not a website mirror, host apply, or branded asset template.
Evidence Fidelity, Structural Fidelity, and Generative Proof are independent required gates; strength in one cannot compensate for failure in another.

mustNot: replace specialist subagents
self-approve Blind QA
invent source evidence
lower frozen thresholds
treat build success as visual success
close a shared-platform incident with a single-brand pass
leave rejected experiments in registry as future learning seeds

fast.purpose: Direction validation for core visual language and two representative demo structures.
fast.evidenceScope: One core viewport plus only goal-critical interactions and assets.
fast.qualityBoundary: May report unresolved secondary states; may not claim complete-style-preview.
fast.stopRule: At 25 minutes stop expanding scope, preserve unresolved evidence, and report the earliest blocker.

full.purpose: Standard learn-brand with responsive evidence, critical motion/assets, generative proof, and Blind QA.
full.evidenceScope: Frozen reference pages, required viewports, high-salience sections, and goal-critical interactions.
full.qualityBoundary: All three proofs must pass before visual-quality-ready.
full.stopRule: At 60 minutes stop adding optional coverage; at 75 minutes block and report the slow node and unresolved evidence instead of exploring indefinitely.

budgetPolicy: Targets are operational budgets, not promises; network, authentication, inaccessible assets, and unusually complex motion may require escalation.
A node that consumes half the profile budget without producing its required artifact must emit a progress receipt and narrow to the frozen goal.
Cache source URL, viewport, asset hash, capture, and interaction traces so retries and additional pages do not repeat unchanged Evidence work.
A QA failure recaptures only affected sections plus required regressions, not the entire source by default.

sectionQualityModel.requiredFor: Every high-salience or goal-critical section on a reference page.
rules: Item count and DOM node count are observations, never substitutes for section structure.
Each required layer has a visible source selector/state and a visible demo selector/state.
Source and Demo captures use the same declared viewport or an approved aspect translation.
Actionable controls must produce an observed state transition; visual-only controls are blocking.
Every high-salience runtime asset has source URL and SHA provenance.
A section may PASS only after its own evidence, structure, responsive behavior, assets, and required interactions pass.
For source-calibration, proof viewport width excludes phone chassis and inspector/showcase gutters; full-bleed surfaces must touch viewport edges while content-safe insets are checked separately.

A standard user-facing Demo route still visibly preserves its phone mockup. No-shell 390px/1440px calibration surfaces are separate and opt-in through an explicit proof mode; proofRole metadata alone must never remove the presentation shell.

externalGoodcaseAdoption.retain: Keep the existing Brand capability when it already enforces a domain-specific hard gate, such as TPP, computed-first evidence, DTCG validation, selector-map, coverage-gate, asset-usage-gate, p0-acceptance, or record-run.
externalGoodcaseAdoption.iterate: Improve an existing Brand capability when the external goodcase offers a better structure, report format, role split, or QA wording without replacing the Brand domain logic.
externalGoodcaseAdoption.deprecate: Remove or merge Brand capability only when it is a Markdown-only duplicate, an outdated synonym, or a softer copy of a stronger script/contract gate.
externalGoodcaseAdoption.optionalHook: Treat external orchestrators as advisory review/QA/retro hooks. Brand Skill must still run without them.

handoffArtifacts.brand-evidence.json: Facts from rendered source: DOM, computed styles, assets, actions, screenshots, and third-party seeds.
handoffArtifacts.brand-intent.json: Meaning and usage guidance for brand patterns. This prevents captured-but-not-understood failures.
handoffArtifacts.design-direction.json: Design Director approval for visual objective, priority order, responsive strategy matrix and independent proof surfaces before implementation.
handoffArtifacts.host-opportunity-map.json: Host page fit analysis. This prevents putting strong C-side visuals into low-capacity efficiency pages.
handoffArtifacts.intent-plan.json: Approved application decision for a specific host project.
handoffArtifacts.visual-qa-report.json: Rendered design review: what looks right, what looks wrong, and what must be downgraded.
handoffArtifacts.visual-comparison-report.json: Source screenshot to demo screenshot comparison. This prevents browser/schema gates from being mistaken for visual learning quality.
handoffArtifacts.generative-proof.json: Proof that evidence-backed invariants can generate a valid variation without mirroring the source composition or relying on an asset swap.
handoffArtifacts.retro-learnings.json: Reusable lessons and their target: script, contract, reference, migration, or host project.
handoffArtifacts.external-goodcase-adoption.json: Decisions for external projects such as gstack: what to retain, iterate, deprecate, or keep as optional hook.

A visually weak demo must be called draft-visual-preview even if registry validation passes.
The Demo is a brand-learning-capability-test, not a website mirror, host apply, or branded asset template.
Evidence Fidelity, Structural Fidelity, and Generative Proof must all pass independently; no aggregate score can compensate for a failed proof.

apply-host.goal: Apply an existing learned visual language into a real host project while preserving host business logic and content.

steps.label: Resolve apply-host intake, source style, and host boundaries
Load existing MOD/style-pack/evidence/intent instead of relearning the demo URL
Read-only diagnosis of host entry, real selector map, visual debt, and current token/component consumption
Classify host page type, visual capacity, Atomic Design layers, asset slots, motion slots, and showcase fit before editing
Freeze a pre-edit structural baseline for every route target after opportunity-map approval and before Host Implementation dispatch
Run TPP blocking gate before applying into host
Map learned intent to host DangoUI/runtime components, preserving host APIs
Apply and verify preview in host project
Review rendered host result for business fit, over-application, C-side expression, and interaction contract quality

onFail.next: return to Evidence, Interpreter/Design Director, or Host Implementation according to cause; then fresh Visual QA

steps.label: Record coverage level, unresolved gaps, and reusable learnings

boundaries: Preserve host route, business content, and component API unless user explicitly asks otherwise.
Do not create a new brand route by default.
Final preview URL must be the host project URL, not the demo URL.
Do not inject showcase moments into low-capacity utility/list/form pages without an explicit business purpose and visualPlacementPolicy.
External orchestration may advise review, but Brand gates decide PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL.

Host Implementation receipt is invalid until the deterministic host theme load-order gate and real rendered selectors/cascade winner proof pass at desktop and mobile, including cold load and route navigation.

Host Implementation receipt is invalid until every edited Vue SFC passes the pre-edit baseline structural diff gate; class/style hooks are allowed but business script, event, route/API, data/state, component API, conditional/loop source and unapproved primitive substitutions are blocked.
Visual QA is read-only; it returns failures to the earliest real Evidence, Interpreter/Design Director or Host Implementation owner and never repairs production code.
No verified DangoUI runtime or component consumer caps mappingStatus at PARTIAL_STYLE_ONLY and wording at conservative-application.

High-capacity placement requires at least three material signals across at least three of visual mass, asset, composition, type and motion; generic palette, archive mood, typography, logos and small icons alone cannot pass.
Report workflowCompletion, businessSafety and visualDistinctiveness separately; never publish a single overall completion percentage.
